title: Environment variables or mounted files
summary: Two ways to hand config to a container, and how each behaves when it changes.

steps.title: Two ways in
body: - configMapRef: { name: shop-config }          # every key becomes an env var
value: debug                                 # explicit env wins over envFrom
mountPath: /app/config                       # each key becomes a file here
ASP.NET Core reads both: environment variables (`Features__NewCheckout=true`, double underscore for `:`) and JSON files you point it at. .NET apps can add `reloadOnChange: true` for files.

steps.prompt: You edit ConfigMap `shop-config` and change `LOG_LEVEL` to `warn`. The pods use it through `envFrom`. When do they see the new value?
options: Only after the pods are restarted (for example `kubectl rollout restart deploy/shop-api`)
steps.explain: Environment variables are fixed when the process starts. Mounted files are refreshed by the kubelet (typically within a minute), unless mounted with `subPath`, which never updates.

items: config the app should hot-reload without restarting
a connection string for a 12-factor app
steps.explain: Files also keep secrets out of `env` output, crash dumps and child processes, which some teams require.

steps.title: Precedence and changes
body: When the same name appears more than once in a container:
envFrom (in list order, later sources win)   <  env (explicit entries win, last one wins)
Common practice so changes roll out safely:
- Put a hash of the config in a pod-template annotation (Helm does this with `checksum/config`). Changing the config changes the template, which triggers a normal **rolling update**.
- Or create a new ConfigMap per version (`shop-config-v7`) and mark them `immutable: true`; rolling back the Deployment then rolls back the config too.
A pod referencing a ConfigMap or Secret key that does not exist fails to start with `CreateContainerConfigError`.

steps.prompt: A pod references `secretKeyRef: { name: shop-db, key: pasword }` (typo). The Secret has only `password`. What STATUS does `kubectl get pods` show?
steps.explain: `kubectl describe pod` shows *couldn't find key pasword in Secret shop/shop-db*. Mark the reference `optional: true` only if the app really copes without it.

steps.prompt: Match the symptom to the cause.
pairs: edited the ConfigMap, pods still log at `info`
values come from env vars; restart needed
mounted file never updates, even after an hour
a referenced ConfigMap/Secret or key is missing
`/app/config` now contains only the ConfigMap files; the image's default files vanished
a volume mounted over an existing directory hides it

steps.prompt: Mount only the `appsettings.json` key of ConfigMap `shop-config` at `/app/config/appsettings.json`.
steps.explain: `items` picks keys and their file names. Mounting a directory (not `subPath`) keeps automatic updates working.

steps.title: Env vars, an override and a config file
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). The ConfigMap `shop-config` holds two settings (`LOG_LEVEL`, `FEATURE_COUPONS`) and a whole file,
`app.json`. The `worker` Deployment loads every key as an environment variable with `envFrom`.
1. `LOG_LEVEL` is `debug` for the worker only (the ConfigMap stays `info` for everyone else);
2. `app.json` is also available as a **file**, `/etc/shop/app.json`, mounted from the same ConfigMap.
Check inside the new pod: `kubectl exec deploy/worker -- printenv LOG_LEVEL` and `... cat /etc/shop/app.json`.

checks.name: LOG_LEVEL is debug in the worker
checks.cmd: kubectl rollout status deploy/worker --timeout=30s >/dev/null && kubectl exec deploy/worker -- printenv LOG_LEVEL FEATURE_COUPONS
checks.fail: In the worker, `LOG_LEVEL` should be `debug` and `FEATURE_COUPONS` still `true`. An `env` entry overrides the same name from `envFrom`.

checks.name: app.json is a file in /etc/shop
checks.fail: `/etc/shop/app.json` is not there. Mount the ConfigMap as a volume (only the `app.json` key, or all of it) at `/etc/shop`.

checks.name: the ConfigMap is unchanged
checks.fail: Leave `shop-config` as it is: the override belongs to the worker.

hints: `kubectl set env deploy/worker LOG_LEVEL=debug` adds an `env` entry; `env` wins over `envFrom`.
A ConfigMap volume: `volumes: [{name: config, configMap: {name: shop-config, items: [{key: app.json, path: app.json}]}}]` and a `volumeMounts` entry at `/etc/shop`.
steps.explain: Environment variables suit single values and are fixed at start; files suit structured config (`appsettings.json`, `nginx.conf`) and are refreshed in place when the ConfigMap changes (unless mounted with `subPath`). Precedence is simple: `envFrom` first, then `env` entries, so a per-workload override never needs a second ConfigMap.
